headline: High risk of prompt injection and cascading errors: ChatGPT Desktop can ingest untrusted files/screenshots while LangGraph can route outputs into actions without built-in verification.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop ingests uploaded files, screenshots, and app content, so attacker-controlled content can reach its prompt. LangGraph is a library that can wire outputs into downstream nodes, creating a plausible bridge if the developer connects them. The pair lacks a documented isolation/provenance layer, but the shared channel is not inherently automatic, so medium fits.
conditions: IF LangGraph nodes consume ChatGPT Desktop outputs as instructions without provenance checks
IF ChatGPT Desktop reads attacker-controlled files or screenshots that LangGraph later forwards
mitigations: Add a strict instruction/data delimiter in the graph prompt template
Require provenance tags on every ChatGPT Desktop output before routing
Disable automatic forwarding of file or screenshot text into agent prompts
Insert a human review step before any tool-using node
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and provenance filtering in the orchestrator

B_data_leakage.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop touches uploaded files, screenshots, voice, and connected IDE code, while LangGraph can persist graph state via a checkpointer store and use developer-defined tools. If the graph stores or forwards ChatGPT-derived content, sensitive data can leak across runs or into model-provider/tool calls. The profiles show a plausible shared-data path, but not an unavoidable exfiltration path, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF ChatGPT Desktop ingests sensitive uploads or screenshots
IF LangGraph persists that content in checkpointer-backed state or sends it to external tools/providers
mitigations: Minimize what LangGraph stores in checkpointer state
Redact secrets from ChatGPT Desktop outputs before persistence
Use separate credentials and workspaces for sensitive tasks
Turn off retention of intermediate agent transcripts where possible
requires-engineering: implement field-level encryption or data-loss-prevention filters

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop has read access to files and clipboard/screen surfaces, while LangGraph can execute shell commands, write files, and spawn subprocesses through developer tools. That overlap creates write/read contention on shared resources if both are pointed at the same workspace. Because the profiles do not guarantee locking or isolation, the conflict is plausible in default orchestration and merits medium severity.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same directory or project state
IF LangGraph tools write files while ChatGPT Desktop reads the same files or app context
mitigations: Assign separate working directories per agent
Serialize file writes through one orchestrator queue
Disable ChatGPT Desktop file access for the shared workspace
Use file locks around any mutable project artifacts
requires-engineering: add transactional state management for shared resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop can produce file-derived or screenshot-derived content, and LangGraph is explicitly a graph of nodes where each node may itself be an agent. That makes it easy for LangGraph to treat ChatGPT output as authoritative and then trigger tool actions or other nodes. Without a documented verification gate, the downstream blast radius can include irreversible actions, so high is warranted.
conditions: IF LangGraph routes ChatGPT Desktop output into an action-taking node
IF no verification or critique step is inserted before tool execution
mitigations: Add a verification node that checks every ChatGPT-derived claim
Require explicit confidence thresholds before tool execution
Log and diff all agent-to-agent handoffs
Block direct action nodes from consuming raw assistant text
requires-engineering: redesign the graph to separate generation from execution

E_compliance.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop touches uploaded files, screenshots, voice, and connected IDE code, while LangGraph handles developer-defined tools and persistent graph state. If regulated data enters ChatGPT and is then persisted or routed through LangGraph, retention and residency obligations can diverge. The profiles do not show a specific residency mismatch, so medium is the highest supportable severity.
conditions: IF regulated data is processed by ChatGPT Desktop
IF LangGraph persists or forwards that data under a different retention or logging policy
mitigations: Classify regulated data before routing it into the pair
Disable persistence for regulated fields in graph state
Review vendor retention settings for ChatGPT Desktop
Keep sensitive workloads in a separate deployment boundary
requires-engineering: align DPA, retention, and residency controls across both systems
